newsitem.title: UK: IPE July Brent ends firmer on NYMEX gasoline rally.
newsitem.headline: IPE July Brent ends firmer on NYMEX gasoline rally.

text.p: IPE July Brent crude oil ended Wednesday firmer in a late NYMEX gasoline-led rally, brokers said.
The prompt July Brent contract closed up 12 cents at $20.12 a barrel, just four cents off the day's high but failed to break above resistance at $20.24.

Earlier bullish statistics from the American Petroleum Institute (API) and U.S Department of Energy (DOE) saw the market firm but with little momentum behind it levels dropped off and locals sold into the contract, brokers said.
"Then it ran out of momentum on the downside and tipped up again. At the end, gasoline took over," one added.
NYMEX unleaded gasoline ended the day 1.01 cents firmer at 66.40 cents, just off the day's high hit late in the session, of 66.60.
The July Brent contract failed to break above flag resistance at $20.24, a close above which could have opened up a run to $21.40 a barrel.

DOE U.S. crude stocks, released on Wednesday, for the week ending May 16 were down some 5.4 million barrels while the overnight API's showed a draw of 5.9 million barrels. Analysts said much of this was disregarded as a large proportion of the draw was in West Coast PADD 5.
Brokers said volume trade on Brent was low for the day and "extremely thin" in the pre-NYMEX trade and added that with the long weekend coming up trade could be quite "volatile" in the next two days.
"With such a strongly NYMEX led market today I would expect London to wait for New York again tomorrow. We expect a slow start to Thursday," another broker said.
June gas oil closed earlier down some $1.50 at $176.50 a tonne.
